plainLanguage: Studies disagree about whether changing your grip width changes how hard the chest muscle works.
qualifiers: The two studies differ in population, load and whether the contraction was isometric or dynamic, so they are not directly comparable.
The elite-athlete null is a non-significant result in twelve participants and cannot distinguish no difference from not enough information.
The 6RM load itself did change with grip width, by 5.8 to 11.1 per cent.

conditions: isometric holds at narrow, mid and wide grips; 6RM sets at three grip widths
scope.population: healthy men and elite male bench press competitors

sourceLinks.locator: Abstract, Results (supinated grip increased clavicular portion activity; narrower grip decreased sternoclavicular portion activity)
Abstract, Results (non-significant activation differences across three grip widths; 6RM loads differed by 5.8-11.1 per cent)
Abstract, Results (clavicular portion activity differed between a 150 and a 50 per cent biacromial grip only in comparison with a machine press)

statement: Evidence on whether bench press grip width changes pectoralis major activation is mixed: one isometric study found grip width and forearm rotation shifted activation between the muscle's portions, while a study of national and international competitors found no significant difference in pectoralis activation across three grip widths at 6RM.
